#Third_Imposed_War #Presence_in_International_Media #International🔰Trump's escalating economic pressure aimed at extracting concessions and reopening the strait will not yield results👤Mohammad Amin Hezrati, senior researcher at the Think Tank's Elite Diplomacy Center, in an interview with Qatar's Al-Arabi network on August 10, examined the quality of Iran-Oman negotiations regarding the Strait of Hormuz and the nature of America's focus on economic pressure against Iran:🔹An examination of the Iran-Oman negotiation process indicates Tehran's strategic transition from viewing the Strait of Hormuz as a hidden power tool toward institutionalizing its leverage. 🔸Tehran no longer sees the Strait of Hormuz merely as a deterrence tool; rather, it is attempting to convert its geopolitical weight and field power into sustainable legal and political arrangements.🔹The main goal is to prevent a return to the status quo and to transform geopolitical influence into tangible rights, balance in economic exploitation, and consolidate Iran's sovereign role in the new structure of the strait.🔸Washington's shift in tactics from military confrontation to economic pressure tools symbolizes "coercive diplomacy" to reduce costs.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank|Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

#Third_Imposed_War #Presence_in_International_Media #Elite_Diplomacy_in_War_80 #International🔰Legal issues and lack of trust are the main political obstacles to the ratification of the Caspian Sea Convention👤Seyed Mohammad Sadegh Emamian, faculty member of Amirkabir University and co-founder of the think tank, in an interview with Azerbaijan's AnewZ on August 12, addressed the political obstacles to advancing bilateral relations between Iran and Azerbaijan:🔹The main obstacle is the lack of trust. Iran has been the target of two rounds of unprovoked aggression by Israel and the United States, which has resulted in heavy civilian costs, including the deaths of hundreds of students.🔸Although political relations between the governments of Tehran and Baku have generally been positive, there was an expectation of a more explicit political stance in support of Iran's national sovereignty and condemnation of the aggressors from the northern neighbors during the recent conflict; a stance that was more clearly expressed by some other neighbors such as Iraq and Pakistan.🔹Recent incidents, including the attack on Iranian ships, showed the absence of strong public condemnation and reinforced historical patterns of mistrust.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank |Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|

#Third_Imposed_War#Presence_in_International_Media#International🔰Contradictory Messages and Efforts to Strike a Balance in the Strait of Hormuz👤Ali Salehian, Director of the Elite Diplomacy Center at the Think Tank, said in an interview with Pakistan's Asia One network on August 5:🔹Trump's public statements about negotiations should be seen primarily as messaging aimed at his domestic MAGA audience. In practice, both sides are simultaneously pursuing military and diplomatic paths to reach an acceptable balance.🔸For Iran, the priority is clear: consolidating sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. This is a security issue rooted in the experience of the February 28 war, not a financial or commercial matter.🔹US threats of more severe military action are unlikely to change Iran's strategy. Tehran faces what it considers an existential threat and is prepared to bear significant costs to protect its national security and sovereignty.🔸The US, in contrast, lacks low-cost military options. A ground operation, an attack on energy, or an attempt to force the reopening of the strait would trigger retaliatory responses from Iran at the regional level.💠Sharif Governance Think Tank|Website| |Telegram Channel| |Bale Channel| |Rubika Channel| |Instagram|
